item.text: [{"taxonId":284707,"summary":"An annual plant native to the Mediterranean and Asia, rocket has deeply lobed leaves and creamy-white flowers marked with purple veins. Its sharp-tasting leaves are widely eaten in salads, while its flowers, young seed pods and mature seeds are also edible.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Leaves, flowers, young pods and mature seeds are edible; leaves are eaten raw or cooked, and aged seed oil is used for salads and cooking.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p3","s1:p4","s1:p20"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p20","s1:p21","s1:p24"]}},{"taxonId":59318,"summary":"A flowering orchid native to western Eurasia and northern Africa, the green-winged orchid usually bears purple flowers, though they may range from white to deep purple. Its green-veined side petals resemble wings, and its flowers produce no nectar.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p9","s1:p2","s1:p14"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":136017,"summary":"A cycad native to Indonesia, New Guinea and Christmas Island, queen sago looks like a palm but is not one. It has glossy, palm-like fronds and grey bark divided by distinctive rectangular or diamond-shaped cracks.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Sago is prepared from dried, ground and washed trunk pith; toxic seeds become edible only after pounding, repeated washing and cooking.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p7"]}},{"taxonId":59005,"summary":"An annual herb native to the Mediterranean Basin, parts of the Middle East and nearby Atlantic islands, tiny bedstraw has very short upright stems with small leaves arranged in whorls.
